chunks: Fadala ibn Ruba' narrated from al-Fadl ibn Zakariyya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Verily, the last one to come out of the Fire will be a man called Hammam, who will call out therein for a lifetime: 'O Compassionate! O Munificent!'

key_terms.حَنَّانُ: Ar-Rahman / The Compassionate (one who shows continuous mercy)
key_terms.مَنَّانُ: Al-Mannan / The Bestower (one who bestows favors abundantly)

ai.seo_question: Who is the last person to leave Hell according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Ahl al-Bayt tradition identifies Hammam as the very last individual to be extracted from Hellfire, highlighting the ultimate extent of divine mercy even for those destined for punishment. His continuous invocation of 'Ya Hannan, Ya Mannan' (O Most Kind, O Bestower of Grace) underscores the Shia emphasis on God's attribute of *Hannan* (continuous kindness) as the mechanism for final intercession. This narrative serves as a theological anchor for the concept of *Khuruj min al-Nar* (exit from Hell), distinguishing it from eternal abode for the majority of sinners.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 6.Faḍālah narrated from Ribʿī, from al-Fuḍayl, from Abū Jaʿfar (a) who said, “
Verily the last one to come out of the Fire will be a man called Hammām, who will call out therein [continually] for a lifetime: ‘O Compassionate! O Munificent!’”
